input.step_by_step_reasoning: 1) Nodes: the World Model lists 6 entities (UserCompanyDeveloper, Route53, ALB, EKS, SNS, SQS). All are kept as individual nodes; the developer is the system entry point (the user of the Orion internal developer platform). Spot instances are drawn next to EKS but appear in the inventory only as a note on EKS, so they are assimilated into the EKS notes rather than added as a separate node. 2) Ledger edges: visual_connections has 5 entries (UserCompanyDeveloper->Route53, Route53->ALB, ALB->EKS, EKS->SNS, SNS->SQS). Each is emitted once with its original direction. 3) Audio-grounded addition: the transcript explicitly says the replacement Kubernetes job 'watches out the AWS SQS' and 'checks SQS if there is anything pending to be processed', so one extra edge EKS->SQS is added as a meta (polling) edge. 4) Flows: flow 0 is the environment-creation request path (developer -> Route53 -> ALB -> EKS). Flow 1 is the job-state resilience path (EKS job emits event to SNS -> SNS fans out to SQS -> replacement job polls SQS). 5) Self-check: visual_connections entries = 5; edges emitted = 6 (5 ledger + 1 explicitly stated in the audio). 6 >= 5.

graph.name: OLX Autos: Orion Internal Developer Platform on Amazon EKS with 100% Spot Instances
graph.categories: Containers, DevOps, Cost Optimization, Application Integration
graph.notes: OLX Autos (operating in 11 countries) built an internal developer platform (Orion portal) to reduce time to market and increase deployment velocity. Users request replica environments; an application pod on Amazon EKS (100% Spot instances) creates one Kubernetes job per microservice. Job state is published through SNS to SQS so that a replacement job can resume unfinished work after a Spot termination.

nodes.name: UserCompanyDeveloper
nodes.notes: End user (developer) who opens the Orion portal to request a new environment, providing the environment name, business use case and business vertical.

nodes.name: Route53
nodes.notes: DNS resolution for the Orion portal URL; resolves to the Application Load Balancer.

nodes.name: ALB
nodes.notes: Application Load Balancer that forwards the request to the Kubernetes pods.

nodes.name: EKS
nodes.notes: Container orchestrator running all workloads. Uses 100% Spot instances for cost efficiency. The main application pod creates one Kubernetes job per microservice (an environment for a business vertical may need 70+ microservices). AWS Node Termination Handler listens for Spot termination events and drains nodes so workloads shift to another node. Scaled from 100 pods to 10,000+ pods.

nodes.name: SNS
nodes.notes: Receives an event whenever a job is triggered to create a microservice and fans the message out to SQS.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Holds job state messages. A replacement job watches the queue to detect unfinished jobs (e.g. a microservice launch interrupted by Spot termination) and completes them, keeping a consistent state for provisioning and maintenance of environments.

edges.notes: User opens the Orion portal URL; DNS resolution goes to Amazon Route 53.
Route 53 resolves the DNS to the Application Load Balancer.
ALB sends the environment-creation request (name, business use case, business vertical) to the application pod running on EKS.
Each Kubernetes job triggered to create a microservice sends an event to Amazon SNS.
SNS fans out the job message to SQS, storing the job state.
The replacement job watches (polls) SQS for unfinished jobs and completes the pending microservice launch.
